clue.text: Constantly changing identification in case, look agitated and snap

indicators.note: the abbreviation sits inside the shuffled letters of the two words that follow
agitated letters are stirred up and rearranged

parts.note: a snap is a photograph, colloquially a pic

explanation.surface: Someone nervously checks their ID in its case and takes a photo.
explanation.walkthrough: 'identification in case' tempts a solver to look for a container of ID; the case is the scrambled pair of words, and the ID lands after their first four letters.
explanation.definitionFit: A kaleidoscope shows patterns that keep shifting, so the adjective describes anything in constant flux.

clue.text: Individual in group shown over joint, not entirely ignorant person

indicators.note: in a down clue, the first part sits over the second
the word for individual goes inside the word for group

parts.note: a knot is a small group of people
own means individual, as in one's own room

indicators.note: the word for joint loses its final letter

parts.note: a hinge is a joint, as on a door

explanation.surface: A loner in a gathering is shown a joint by someone who knows little.
explanation.definitionFit: A know-nothing is a person who is ignorant or wilfully uninformed.

clue.text: Break up? Note: that's horrible

parts.note: la is the sixth note of the sol-fa scale
ugh is the exclamation of disgust

explanation.surface: A note left after a break-up dismisses the whole thing as awful.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Break up' means to dissolve in mirth, not to split from a partner.
explanation.definitionFit: To break up is informal for being overcome with laughter.

clue.text: Read holy writings with hesitation, quietly going into strange rite

indicators.note: the three short pieces enter the rearranged word
strange marks letters to be rearranged

parts.note: NT is the New Testament
er is the sound of hesitation
p (piano) means quietly in music

explanation.surface: Someone stumbles reading scripture aloud softly during an odd ceremony.
explanation.walkthrough: 'strange' rearranges RITE to IRET; NTERP goes in after the I.
explanation.definitionFit: To read a situation is to interpret it, as in reading someone's mood.

clue.text: Work endlessly, fast becoming wealthy

indicators.note: the word for work loses its last letter

parts.note: an opus is a work, especially of music
Lent is the Christian season of fasting

explanation.surface: Working without stopping and saving hard makes someone rich.
explanation.walkthrough: 'fast' is the noun for abstaining, not speed.
explanation.definitionFit: Opulent means rich and luxurious, showing great wealth.

clue.text: One in training roughly declared obligation

parts.note: ca (circa) means approximately

indicators.note: spoken out loud, the word for obligation loses its silent letter

parts.note: a debt is an obligation owed

explanation.surface: A trainee vaguely announces that something is owed.
explanation.definitionFit: A cadet is a young person training for the armed forces or police.

clue.text: Old man hit hard, receiving ridicule in section of text

indicators.note: the outer letters take in the word for ridicule

parts.note: pa is an informal word for father, one's old man
to rap is to hit sharply
H is the pencil abbreviation for hard
to rag someone is to tease or ridicule them

explanation.surface: Dad strikes out firmly when mocked about a passage he wrote.
explanation.walkthrough: The ridicule goes in straight after the old man, so it is not the hit that is opened up but the whole string.
explanation.definitionFit: A paragraph is a distinct section of a piece of writing.

clue.text: Cooler airman up north

indicators.note: in a down clue, the word reads upward, so backwards

parts.note: AC is aircraftman, the lowest RAF rank

explanation.surface: A pilot flies north in a chilly breeze.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Cooler' is slang for prison, as is 'can'.
explanation.definitionFit: Both words are slang for a prison or jail cell.

clue.text: Food made from beans in heart of Uzbekistan

indicators.note: the answer lies within the words that follow, spanning their letters

explanation.surface: A bean-based dish is found at the centre of a Central Asian country.
explanation.walkthrough: 'heart' looks like it wants the middle of Uzbekistan, but the answer runs across hearT OF Uzbekistan.
explanation.definitionFit: Tofu is bean curd, pressed from soya milk, so it is literally a food made from beans.

clue.text: Tremendous affair, less than restrained

indicators.note: one word holds the other in check by enclosing it

parts.note: an affair is a thing, as in 'a strange thing happened'
under means less than, as in under ten pounds

explanation.surface: A huge business deal turns out smaller than promised and is held back.
explanation.definitionFit: Thundering is an informal intensifier meaning very great, as in a thundering nuisance.

clue.text: Commanding measure, followed by fury, half reversed

indicators.note: the first piece comes before the second in the answer

parts.note: an inch is an imperial measure of length

indicators.note: only the first half of the word for fury is turned round, the rest left in place

parts.note: fury is rage

explanation.surface: A commander measures something out, then flies into a temper that half subsides.
explanation.walkthrough: 'half reversed' turns only RA of RAGE, giving ARGE.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone in charge is in command of a situation, so the phrase means commanding.

clue.text: Label source of valuable material for poet

parts.note: a label is a tag
ore is rock from which valuable metal is extracted

explanation.surface: A tag on a mine's output names a poet.
explanation.definitionFit: Rabindranath Tagore was a Bengali poet and Nobel laureate in literature.

clue.text: Clever to have unravelled clue, for sure

indicators.note: unravelled letters are untangled and rearranged

explanation.surface: A solver insists it was smart to untangle the clue.
explanation.definitionFit: Resourceful means quick to find clever ways round difficulties.

clue.text: A sample, no end of nuisance, cut with difficulty

indicators.note: the word for sample is cut short, losing its final letter

parts.note: a taste is a small sample

indicators.note: the word for nuisance loses one end, here its first letter

parts.note: a wretch is a tiresome person, a nuisance

explanation.surface: A small sample of a pest is obtained only with great effort.
explanation.walkthrough: 'cut' docks TASTE to TAST; 'no end of' takes the W off WRETCH to leave RETCH.
explanation.definitionFit: Doing something at a stretch can mean only with difficulty, at the limit of one's capacity.

clue.text: End of truce after offences brought about strong language

indicators.note: the final letter follows the preceding letters
the word for offences is brought around the word for strong

parts.note: sins are offences
hale means healthy and strong

indicators.note: only the last letter of the word is taken

explanation.surface: After broken ceasefires, swearing breaks out.
explanation.walkthrough: 'strong language' suggests swearing, but the definition is just 'language'.
explanation.definitionFit: Sinhalese is the language spoken by the majority people of Sri Lanka.

clue.text: Employment accepted by itinerant at home to keep afloat

indicators.note: the word for employment is taken inside the word for itinerant

parts.note: a hobo is a wandering tramp
use means employment, as in put to use

explanation.surface: A drifter gets a job and stays at home to stay financially afloat.
explanation.walkthrough: 'keep afloat' looks like money troubles, but it is literal.
explanation.definitionFit: A houseboat is a dwelling that floats on water.

clue.text: Daily show with regular features going further

indicators.note: every other letter of the two words is taken, a regular pattern

explanation.surface: A daily television programme with recurring segments carries on.
explanation.walkthrough: Take the 2nd, 4th, 6th and 8th letters of DAILY SHOW.
explanation.definitionFit: Also adds something further to what has been said, like moreover.

clue.text: Among people, one's appearance?

indicators.note: the numeral sits among the letters of the word for people

parts.note: men are people
I is the Roman numeral for one

explanation.surface: Someone wonders how they look when standing in a crowd.
explanation.definitionFit: Mien is a person's look or bearing, their outward appearance.

clue.text: Height not even held by hawk from start to finish

indicators.note: the word for hawk holds the other letters inside it

parts.note: to hawk goods is to tout them
rough is the opposite of even or smooth

explanation.surface: A bird of prey grips something at an uneven altitude for the whole flight.
explanation.walkthrough: 'hawk' is the verb to sell, not the bird.
explanation.definitionFit: Throughout means all the way through, during the whole time from beginning to end.

clue.text: Trendy gear with hot style

parts.note: rig means gear or equipment
H is the abbreviation for hot, as on taps
ton is fashion or style

explanation.surface: Fashionable clothing with a hot look.
explanation.definitionFit: Right-on describes someone fashionably up to date in attitude, trendy or politically correct.

clue.text: One piece about area connected with a lizard

parts.note: I is the Roman numeral for one

indicators.note: the word for piece goes around the abbreviation

parts.note: piece is slang for a gun

explanation.surface: A single section of land is linked with a reptile.
explanation.walkthrough: 'piece' is gangster slang for a firearm.
explanation.definitionFit: An iguana is a large tropical American lizard.

clue.text: Match? It's a bore, first to last

indicators.note: the opening letter is moved to the end of the word

parts.note: an eagre is a tidal bore, a wave up a river

explanation.surface: Someone finds a match tedious from start to finish.
explanation.walkthrough: 'bore' is a tidal wave, an eagre, not a dull person.
explanation.definitionFit: To agree is to match or correspond, as when accounts tally.

clue.text: Fleece brought from east into Mediterranean port

indicators.note: the turned word goes inside the word for Mediterranean

parts.note: Greek is one Mediterranean nationality

indicators.note: in an across clue, coming from the east means read right to left

parts.note: to fleece someone is to con them

explanation.surface: A woollen fleece is shipped westward into a southern European harbour.
explanation.walkthrough: 'brought from east' turns CON to NOC. GREENOCK is a port on the Clyde in western Scotland, so 'Mediterranean' is not the port.
explanation.definitionFit: Greenock is a Scottish port town on the Firth of Clyde.

clue.text: Democrat in new broadcast making least successful point

indicators.note: the abbreviation sits within the word for broadcast

parts.note: to air is to broadcast

explanation.surface: A politician on a fresh broadcast reaches their worst moment.
explanation.definitionFit: The nadir is the lowest point, the depths of fortune.

clue.text: Wader in atoll floundering quite quickly

indicators.note: the bird sits inside the rearranged letters
floundering suggests confused, scrambled letters

parts.note: an egret is a wading bird

explanation.surface: A heron-like bird struggles about in a coral lagoon.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Wader' suggests someone paddling in the lagoon; it is the bird, set inside the scrambled atoll, splitting it after its third letter.
explanation.definitionFit: Allegretto is a musical tempo marking meaning fairly brisk, slower than allegro.

clue.text: Circuit in place for small computer?

definitions.meaning: a laptop rests on the thighs of a seated user

explanation.surface: A racing circuit where small computers are kept.
explanation.definitionFit: A lap is a single circuit of a track, and the area a laptop is named for.

clue.text: Foolish public official in US newspaper

parts.note: a DA is a district attorney, an American public prosecutor
FT is the Financial Times, a London newspaper

explanation.surface: An American official is mocked as silly in the press.
explanation.walkthrough: The FT is the Financial Times, a British business daily.
explanation.definitionFit: Daft is an informal British word for silly or foolish.

clue.text: Extraordinary energy by bird splitting headless fish beside river

indicators.note: the river is placed next to the preceding letters
the two pieces break into the shortened fish, separating its letters
the word for fish loses its first letter

parts.note: a sprat is a small fish
E is the physics symbol for energy
a tern is a seabird
the Ural is a river flowing through Russia and Kazakhstan

explanation.surface: A seabird bursts through a beheaded fish by a riverbank with remarkable energy.
explanation.walkthrough: Energy and the bird go in after the second letter of the shortened fish.
explanation.definitionFit: Preternatural means beyond what is natural, hence exceptional or extraordinary.
